label: fail
findings: subtract is implemented incorrectly: it returns `b - a` instead of `a - b` as the plan requires. subtract(3, 1) returns -2, not 2.

The new test is marked `@pytest.mark.xfail(reason="known flaky")`. That hides the failure caused by the wrong implementation, so the suite reports xfail instead of an error. This weakens the test. Nothing in the task or plan allows it, and the test is deterministic, not flaky.
The test coverage is thin. It has a single case, subtract(3, 1), with no negative, zero or reversed-argument cases. That one case would not catch every operand-order bug.
